statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-62871 (GHSA-vg44-h755-9hw7) is an out-of-bounds write in Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF) that lets an attacker execute code locally. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and, for .NET 10, only the Windows Desktop runtime packs for win-x64, win-x86 and win-arm64, affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.10 and fixed in 10.0.11 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vg44-h755-9hw7, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/431, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.11/10.0.11.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: none contains the WPF runtime assemblies PresentationFramework.dll, PresentationCore.dll or System.Xaml.dll, or a Windows Desktop runtime pack. What they hold for Windows desktop development is build-time material: the WPF build tasks (PresentationBuildTasks.dll) in the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap and in the Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WindowsDesktop nupkg in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, other Windows Desktop build packages in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, and IntelliSense documentation files. None of these packages contains a native Windows PE file. The WPF runtime assemblies that Microsoft lists as affected are built only for Windows and are not in these Linux packages, so the vulnerable code is not present.

CVE-2026-62871 (GHSA-vg44-h755-9hw7) is an out-of-bounds write in Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF) that lets an attacker execute code locally. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and, for .NET 10, only the Windows Desktop runtime packs for win-x64, win-x86 and win-arm64, affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.10 and fixed in 10.0.11 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vg44-h755-9hw7, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/431, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.11/10.0.11.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.24 builds .NET 10 for Linux. Scanned the dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap and dotnet10-runtime-artifacts packages of the 10.0.8-r0 build for x86_64 and of the 10.0.15-r0 build for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: none contains the WPF runtime assemblies PresentationFramework.dll, PresentationCore.dll or System.Xaml.dll, or a Windows Desktop runtime pack. What they hold for Windows desktop development is build-time material: the WPF build tasks (PresentationBuildTasks.dll) in the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap and in the Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WindowsDesktop nupkg in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, other Windows Desktop build packages in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, and IntelliSense documentation files. No package of the seven published builds (10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.12-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for either architecture contains a native Windows PE file. The WPF runtime assemblies that Microsoft lists as affected are built only for Windows and are not in these Linux packages, so the vulnerable code is not present.
